references.text: The same chapter describes the sin offering for the anointed priest, which also requires a young bull as a sin offering.
Describes how the priest is to make atonement for the congregation with the bull, and that the sin will be forgiven.
Parallel text about the congregation's sin offering when they sin unintentionally, with a young bull as a burnt offering.
The offering must be brought before the Lord's presence at the entrance of the tent of meeting, the same place mentioned in the verse.
The expression 'when the sin becomes known' is repeated here for a ruler's sin offering.
Deals with when a person becomes aware of their sin and must confess it, similar to the concept of acknowledging sin.
Hebrews refers to the sin offering that the high priest brought forward for sins committed by the people in ignorance.
Explains that the high priest must bring an offering for the people's sins, which points back to this sacrificial system.
